chapter: Billy Bauer, George Russell and Charlie Parker
title: Jackie McLean's tribute to Parker's 'Lover Man'
summary: They discuss McLean reproducing Parker's sick 'Lover Man' solo and Parker's health.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: Jackie McLean told a story once about how Miles reamed him out because Jackie didn’t know “Yesterdays” and Jackie said: “I’m young, I’ll learn it later” and Miles just jumped down his throat. Apparently “Yesterdays” was important to Miles for whatever reason.

Do you know that I heard Jackie at the Blue Note introduce the fact that he “is now going to play Charlie Parker’s version of ‘Lover Man’”, the ill-fated “Lover Man” where he went to Camarillo. Jackie McLean

That was after he fell asleep and set fire to the room and ran out into the lobby of the hotel naked and they came and took him to jail and then sent him to Camarillo. So he [Jackie McLean] recreated Bird’s solo on that tune?
He played that same sad-assed sound and everything. I’d say that was really weird.
I heard him, I was sitting there. I said: “What is he doing?” But it was very dramatic the way he did it.
It was the worst record he ever made.
He would never have appreciated that tribute.
Yeah I don’t think so, although, some people seem to think it sounds soulful or something. It sounds like a sick man.

Yeah. To that extent it was soulful. We knew how sick he was but it wasn’t done to the heading of great music because everything he tried to play he could play when he was not sick and was not much better so it just sounded sad.
Exactly. Supposedly they were propping him up, literally, against the mic so he could play. His health was that bad at the point.
